questions.stem: What is the direction of friction relative to the motion of an object?

options.text: In the same direction as motion
Opposite to the direction of motion
Perpendicular to the direction of motion

questions.explanation: Friction is a resistive force that always acts in the opposite direction to the motion (or attempted motion) of an object. It opposes the relative movement between two surfaces in contact.

questions.stem: What happens to the drag force on an object as its speed increases?
questions.explanation: Drag force (air resistance) increases as an object moves faster. This is why a falling object eventually reaches terminal velocity -- the drag force increases until it equals the weight.
